Device Query Conformance Tests

The opt-in query suite checks the Device Interface property contracts in include/qdmi/device.h and include/qdmi/constants.h. It compiles against a provider's prefixed symbols and runs through GoogleTest. It creates no jobs and makes no provider network calls. Supply a controlled local fixture; a fixture that connects to hardware is outside this suite's offline guarantees.

Integration

Use CMake 3.24 or newer and a C++20 compiler. Supply GoogleTest with an existing GTest::gtest_main target and enable CTest in the consuming project. QDMI neither fetches GoogleTest nor enables tests when this helper is merely included. add_subdirectory exposes the helper from a source checkout; find_package(qdmi CONFIG REQUIRED) exposes the same helper and test source from an installation. QDMI's own tests, examples, and templates may all be disabled.

The installation must include the query helper. Older QDMI releases may satisfy the package version check without providing add_qdmi_device_query_tests.

find_package(qdmi CONFIG REQUIRED)
find_package(GTest CONFIG REQUIRED)
enable_testing()
# my-device already supplies MY-prefixed headers and device symbols.
add_qdmi_device_query_tests(
my-query-tests
PREFIX MY
TARGET my-device
FIXTURE_HEADER "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/query_fixture.hpp")

PREFIX is the exact device symbol prefix. TARGET supplies the device library and its public include directories. FIXTURE_HEADER is an existing header; relative paths are resolved against the caller's source directory. Paths may contain spaces. Invoke the helper with distinct executable names to test several devices. On Windows, the helper copies a shared device target's DLL beside the test executable. Other runtime dependencies remain the consumer's responsibility. Tests have distinct executable-name prefixes and the CTest label qdmi-query.

The header defines QDMIQueryFixture, derived from ::testing::Test, with a protected initialized session named session of the prefixed session type. Initialize the device once in SetUpTestSuite, allocate and initialize a session in SetUp, free it in TearDown, and finalize the device in TearDownTestSuite. Check setup errors with GoogleTest assertions and make cleanup safe after partial setup. GoogleTest supplies main; do not define another one. See test/query/example_fixture.hpp for a complete offline example, and test/query/consumer for a separate consumer project.

cmake --build build --target my-query-tests
ctest --test-dir build -L qdmi-query --output-on-failure

Dependency configuration may download packages. Test execution needs no credentials or provider access. The example's token is only a local placeholder. Ordinary consumers that do not call the helper acquire no query executable or GoogleTest dependency.

Checked Contracts

For each supported property the suite checks support-only and size-only queries, exact and oversized typed buffers, optional size_ret, and one-byte-short buffers. It validates scalar types, string termination, array element sizes, defined enum values, and advertised nonnull handles. Invalid enums, removed device property IDs 8 and 9, and isolated null arguments are checked against the specified errors. Error returns may overwrite the supplied buffer.

Each of the 51 contract checks runs as four separate GoogleTest cases: exact and oversized buffers, each with and without size_ret. Each case validates its retrieved values and relationships before another retrieval can replace them. Test names identify the variant as ExactWithoutSize, ExactWithSize, OversizedWithoutSize, or OversizedWithSize.

Device coverage includes name, version, library version, ID, status, qubit count, queue length, site and operation lists, coupling map, child devices, supported program formats, length and duration units and scale factors, and minimum atom distance. Site coverage includes name, mandatory index, T1, T2, coordinates, zone status, spatial extents, module index, and submodule index. Operation coverage includes name, qubit and parameter counts, duration, fidelity, interaction and blocking radii, idling fidelity, zone status, site tuples, and mean shuttling speed. Relationships include distinct site indices and supported coordinate triples, coupling endpoints in advertised sites, and conditional unit availability. The installed headers remain the normative reference.

Optional unsupported properties skip when no advertised object supports them. Mixed support across objects is valid; mandatory site index support is checked on every advertised site. Empty arrays and sparse indices are valid. Site counts need not equal qubit counts, since sites may represent zones. Direct device ID support is optional; the client-visible stable-ID rule is separate. Repeated metadata values need not stay equal. Metadata growth during retrieval is reported explicitly; use controlled metadata for reproducible results. Payloads above the suite's 64 MiB allocation limit fail with a diagnostic; that is a harness limit, not a QDMI size restriction.

Exclusions and Specification Follow-up

The suite does not create jobs, compile programs, set session parameters, load providers, or validate credentials. It does not probe fabricated, foreign, freed, or uninitialized handles. Custom properties have implementation-defined types and are excluded. Operation queries use zero site and parameter counts with null inputs; context-dependent metadata is excluded. It adds no undocumented numerical bounds, gate names, ordering, or topology symmetry requirements.

The suite assumes valid native scalar object representations. ABI-invalid or memory-corrupting providers require separate memory-safety and sanitizer checks. Payload-shape and value checks do not prove that every successful query wrote its full payload. Buffer-overrun detection belongs to separate memory-safety testing.

Unit strings are checked for shape, conditional availability, and the canonical symbols specified in the headers. Radius and idling-fidelity applicability and zero-arity local-operation tuple semantics also need clarification before adding stronger assertions. The suite does not change the normative API docstrings.

QDMI CI runs positive controls and fixed negative controls for malformed sizes, invalid device properties, empty units, missing mandatory indices, omitted size outputs, invalid status values, missing string terminators, null advertised handles, and duplicate coordinate triples in every retrieval variant. Positive controls cover empty and valid handle lists, integer coordinate extremes, differences on each coordinate axis, and partial coordinate support. It also runs source and relocated installed consumers on Linux and macOS. The consumer checks include fixture/install paths with spaces and explicit opt-out. This workflow does not run on Windows; local Windows verification is separate.
